subject: [COMPANY] <> Encord
text:
Hi [NAME], 

       I've been following 
       [COMPANY]'s work on GenAI and safe agentic systems, especially your focus on reliability across global use cases. 

       We're working with regulated AI teams like Veriff, Onfido, VIDA who've found that as GenAI scales across regions and BUs, lightweight labeling tools start to break down - especially around multimodal data (image, text, video, audio), multilingual support, and model eval feedback loop. That's where Encord tends to fit in.

       Given your role leading AI and data, I'd value the chance to compare notes. 

       Open to a quick chat next week?

subject: [NAME] - ML ops
text:
Hi [NAME], 

       I've been chatting with a few ML engineers in fraud/IDV teams and a common theme keeps coming up - the real bottleneck isn't modeling, it's data prep, edge case surfacing, and making eval loops less painful. 

       I'm curious how that looks on your side at 
       [COMPANY]. 

       At Encord, we work pretty closely with teams in the weeds on things like curation, annotation, QA, and eval workflows - especially around identifying failure modes and tightening feedback loops without adding more manual overhead. 

       Would you be open to a quick 20 min chat to compare notes? Tues - Thurs works well for me, but I'm happy to work around you.

subject: new tool
text:
Hi [NAME], 

        I know you're close to the Label Studio ecosystem, so I'll be straightforward. Encord is a natural next step for teams that have outgrown it. 

        We've recently transitioned a few teams off them that are working with native surgical video and DICOM workflows, and the inflection point is usually around the need for more complex ontologies, multimodal support, agents/model-assisted pre-labeling, scalable QA, and more standardized data ingestion/export setups. 

        Not assuming that's what you need at this point - but if scaling your data pipeline is on eht road map, I'd love a quick call to introduce you to Encord.
